title: Cost-SLO Playbook (scratch)
content:
Context:
- Quick personal scratchpad for a lightweight playbook to enforce Cost SLOs for Redwood hosted inference customers and for internal feature rollouts. Not a polished doc, just a place to capture concrete ideas and experiments.
- Why: teams keep asking for predictable inference spend. We have knobs (batching, quantization, routing, dedicated pools) but no small playbook that PS/CS can run to get customers within a target $/request SLA.

Top-level goal:
- Help customers hit a target cost-per-inference percentile (e.g., p95 cost per request <= $0.006) while maintaining latency SLOs and quality.
- Secondary: create a repeatable runbook for Solutions Eng and CS to use during onboarding and incident reviews.

Audience:
- Solutions/CS onboarding leads
- PL/engineers running hosted API in production
- Internal PM/Eng wanting to evaluate customer cost regressions

Constraints / assumptions:
- Customers can opt into suggested optimizations; some require model changes or dedicated capacity.
- We prioritize non-invasive changes first (routing, batching, cache) then model-level (quantization, smaller model variants).
- Must provide measurable rollback/fallback if quality drops.

High-level playbook outline (staged):
1) Baseline measurement (2–3 days)
   - Collect per-route token counts, model variant, qps, p50/p95 latency, and cost per token.
   - Identify tail calls > target cost or latency.
   - Output: baseline report with top 10 routes by cost impact.

2) Quick wins (1 week)
   - Prefix caching for repeated prompts (enable and measure hit rate)
   - Adjust batching thresholds (smaller batches for latency-sensitive routes; larger for background jobs)
   - Route low-priority requests to cheaper model variant or lower precision if available
   - Output: delta report, projected monthly savings, any latency/quality regressions observed

3) Model-level optimizations (2–4 weeks)
   - Enable quantized variant where available; run A/B evaluation on quality metrics with held-out prompts
   - Introduce candidate smaller model for specific routes with SLA gating
   - Output: rollout plan with guardrails, rollback triggers, quality thresholds

4) Dedicated capacity discussions (parallel)
   - For customers with sustained high qps, evaluate Dedicated reservation to reduce unit cost
   - Provide comparison: hosted per-token vs dedicated committed monthly cost (TCO sheet)

5) Monitoring & continuous guardrails (ongoing)
   - Alerts for cost-per-request drift > X% week-over-week
   - Automated nightly job that suggests config diffs (batch size, cache TTL) with one-click apply in Console (pm idea)

User stories (rough):
- As a Solutions Engineer, I want a short checklist I can run in the first 2 weeks of onboarding that reduces customer cost by ~15% without model changes.
- As a product manager, I want a dashboard that surfaces top 5 routes by cost impact and recommended action (cache/batch/route) so I can prioritize work.
- As an SRE, I want rollback windows and automated quality gates on quantization rollouts to avoid user-visible regressions.

Acceptance criteria (MVP):
- A template baseline report (CSV + summary) that pulls from Console usage APIs.
- A 2-page checklist for SEs with commands/Console links for enabling prefix cache, changing batching policy, and routing rules.
- Two experiment templates: (A) quantization A/B with quality metric capture, (B) route-to-cheaper-model canary with traffic split.
- Automated alert configured in Console for cost-per-request drift > 20% within 7d.

Quick experiment ideas (one-offs to test):
- Short-term: Increase batching window on non-interactive endpoints by 50ms and measure cost delta and p95 latency.
- Medium-term: Deploy 4-bit quantized variant for reranker model in a canary (5% traffic), compare precision@1 on stored eval set.
- Non-invasive: Add a header-based routing rule for known low-quality prompts to always hit larger model; inverse for high-volume boilerplate prompts.

Metrics to track (minimum):
- Cost per request (mean, p50, p95) by route and model variant
- Latency p50/p95 by route
- Cache hit rate (prefix + KV)
- Quality regression proxies (eval score, user error rate if available)
- Monthly committed vs hosted unit cost (for Dedicated evaluation)

Open questions / risks:
- What is the smallest safe quality delta for quantization (we need concrete thresholds per model family).
- Billing visibility: can Console provide per-route chargebacks at token granularity? If not, SE process more manual.
- How invasive is prefix caching for prompt templates that include user state (privacy/consent concerns)? Need legal check for reuse of customer data across requests.

Parking lot (nice-to-have):
- One-click "Cost SLO optimizer" in Console that proposes candidate optimizations and simulates monthly savings before applying.
- SDK-level helper that suggests optimal batch size based on observed interarrival times.
- Predefined "cost profiles" customers can opt into (latency-first, cost-first, balanced).

Implementation notes (engineer-facing):
- Baseline collector should be a lightweight job that queries usage telemetry and model labels; export CSV with route, model, tokens, cost, latency.
- Recommend adding a flag in rollout system for "cost-guardrails" to prevent simultaneous quantization + routing changes without explicit approval.

Next steps / immediate TODOs (for me):
- Draft a 1-pager checklist and share with Maya for feedback (target: next Tue).
- Wireframe a baseline report layout and ask Liam for a quick script that pulls Console usage data.
- Add legal question about prefix caching to the queue and tag for follow-up.

Meeting notes (from quick sync with Maya 2025-01-21):
- Maya: SEs need prescriptive language (exact commands) not high-level advice.
- Agreed action: produce a sample email template for customers explaining quantization canary and rollback plan.

Tiny ideas to keep for later:
- "Cost SLO badge" customers can enable which shows a green/yellow/red in Console based on their 7d trend.
- Auto-suggest after 10k requests/day: "You may save $X/month by switching to dedicated" slide in the billing page.

---
End of scratch notes. Will iterate into a tidy playbook when baseline collector exists and we have SE feedback.
